project.name: screenpipe
project.description: screenpipe is a local-first context infrastructure project that records screen and audio activity so users can rewind, ask, search, and automate against their private activity history. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

layers.name: Desktop UI
layers.description: Next.js and React surfaces for the screenpipe desktop application, including pages, components, hooks, and client-side app behavior.

layers.description: Native Tauri application code, commands, permissions, and macOS or desktop integration logic that hosts the UI and local services.

layers.name: Capture & AI Pipelines
layers.description: Screen, audio, OCR, accessibility, transcription, redaction, and Apple Intelligence crates that collect and transform local user context.

layers.name: Core Server & Storage
layers.description: Rust backend, database, configuration, events, vault, and engine code that stores local context and serves it to clients and agents.

layers.name: Integrations & Packages
layers.description: MCP, browser extension, AI gateway, SDK, and package-level integrations that expose screenpipe data outside the desktop runtime.

layers.name: Tests & Evaluation
layers.description: End-to-end tests, benchmarks, evaluation crates, test fixtures, and validation assets used to protect capture quality and product stability.

layers.name: Data Schemas
layers.description: SQL migrations, schemas, and structured data definitions that describe persisted screenpipe state and supporting datasets.

layers.name: Infrastructure & CI
layers.description: Docker, GitHub Actions, release automation, setup scripts, and deployment infrastructure for building and shipping screenpipe.

layers.name: Configuration & Tooling
layers.description: Project manifests, formatter settings, build configuration, and tool-specific files that configure the monorepo.

layers.name: Documentation & Product
layers.description: Product vision, contribution docs, user guides, and repository documentation that explain how screenpipe should be used and evolved.

tour.title: Project Purpose
tour.description: Start with the README and vision documents to anchor the codebase around the product promise: local screen and audio context for AI agents. These files explain why stability, local-first data handling, and the Record/Rewind/Ask workflow shape the rest of the architecture.

tour.title: Desktop Surface
tour.description: The desktop app starts from the Next.js app surface and shared layout. This layer is where users interact with recording, rewind, settings, and ask flows before requests cross into native Tauri or local APIs.

tour.title: Client Utilities
tour.description: The frontend depends heavily on shared API, settings, toast, and Tauri helper modules. Reading these files after the app entry points shows how UI state and commands are normalized before they reach native or backend code.

tour.title: Native Runtime
tour.description: The Tauri runtime is the bridge between the web UI and the local machine. It wires app startup, native commands, permissions, sidecars, and desktop-specific behavior that make screenpipe run as a long-lived background application.

tour.title: Capture Stack
tour.description: The capture crates collect the raw context screenpipe exists to preserve: screen state, accessibility text, audio, OCR, and redaction. This step connects the product promise from Step 1 to the low-level data acquisition code.

tour.title: Engine Server
tour.description: The engine and server code coordinates local processing and exposes the API used by the desktop app and external agents. This is the place to understand how captured context becomes queryable application behavior.

tour.title: Storage Model
tour.description: The database crate and migrations define how frames, audio transcripts, UI events, and redaction state are persisted locally. This layer is central to rewind, search, retention, and privacy-sensitive cleanup behavior.

tour.title: Agent Integrations
tour.description: The integration packages expose screenpipe context to external surfaces such as MCP, browser automation, and AI gateway code. This step shows how the local memory layer becomes useful to agents beyond the desktop UI.

tour.title: Event Flow
tour.description: Events, connections, and vault/secrets modules provide the cross-cutting runtime plumbing around capture and automation. Read these after the core server and integrations to see how state changes and secure local configuration move through the system.

tour.title: Regression Safety
tour.description: The testing guide and E2E package encode the regression history for permissions, tray behavior, recording, settings, and lifecycle flows. This is the practical checkpoint before changing window management, capture, audio, or Apple Intelligence behavior.

tour.title: Release Pipeline
tour.description: GitHub Actions and Docker files describe how screenpipe is tested, packaged, and released across app, CLI, browser extension, and MCP surfaces. Finish here to understand the operational path from code change to shipped artifact.

tour.title: Workspace Configuration
tour.description: The workspace manifests and formatter/test configuration define the development envelope for the monorepo. These files are useful reference points when adding crates, packages, or automation that must fit the existing build and tooling model.
